questions.q: Why would you branch before reworking the grain of a dbt model that feeds production dashboards?
options: Branches make your SQL queries run faster
Branching is required by Git before any commit can happen
There is no reason — branching is purely optional busywork
Committing directly on main would expose your half-finished, possibly broken work to everyone using the project immediately
questions.explain: A branch keeps risky, in-progress work isolated from main until it's ready, so production dashboards aren't affected mid-change.

questions.q: What does git switch -c rework-ltv-grain do?
options: Renames the main branch
Creates a new branch called rework-ltv-grain and switches to it in one step
Deletes the current branch
Merges rework-ltv-grain into main immediately
questions.explain: -c tells git switch to create the named branch and check it out immediately, equivalent to git checkout -b.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what happens to main while you commit on a separate branch?
options: main is automatically updated with every commit you make
main and your branch merge automatically after every commit
main is deleted
main doesn't move — your branch's commits only extend that branch's own line of history
questions.explain: Commits on a branch only extend that branch; main stays exactly where it was until you explicitly merge or rebase.

questions.q: What happens to your in-progress schema-rework commits when you run git switch main?
options: Git refuses to switch branches if there are any commits
They are automatically merged into main
Nothing is lost — they're safely committed on the other branch, just not currently checked out
They are permanently deleted
questions.explain: Switching branches changes which commits are checked out on disk; committed work on the other branch remains intact and waiting.

questions.q: What does running git branch with no arguments do?
options: Pushes all branches to GitHub
Creates a new branch with a random name
Lists every branch you have and marks the current one with an asterisk
Deletes all branches except main
questions.explain: git branch with no arguments simply lists local branches, marking the currently checked-out one with an asterisk.
